context: Tests whether the agent detects a partially-built workspace and resumes it rather than starting over, preserving files that already exist and re-asking nothing that is already on record. Setup is destructive if done wrong: clobbering cv-base.yaml loses the user's career facts.

checklist.name: Detected the existing workspace
checklist.description: Explicitly reports that a workspace already existed and was incomplete, rather than treating this as a fresh setup

checklist.name: Preserved identity.md
checklist.description: The existing identity.md is not overwritten: name is still Ada Lovelace and email is still ada@example.com

checklist.name: Did not re-ask known facts
checklist.description: Does not ask the user for the name, email, or phone that were already present in identity.md

checklist.name: Filled the identity gaps
checklist.description: The previously empty address_line_1, city, and postcode are filled from what the user supplied

checklist.name: Created the missing profile files
checklist.description: logistics.md, targets.md, narrative.md, and demographics.md all now exist

checklist.name: Built cv-base.yaml
checklist.description: cv/cv-base.yaml exists and contains all seven employers named in the prompt

checklist.name: Created at least one track
checklist.description: At least one file exists under cv/tracks/, matching the forward-deployed-engineer target the user stated

checklist.name: Preserved the log header
checklist.description: applications/log.csv still has exactly one header row, not duplicated and not replaced

checklist.name: Logistics recorded correctly
checklist.description: logistics.md records requires_sponsorship as no, notice_period as one month, and a salary expectation around 110000 GBP

checklist.name: Demographics default to declining
checklist.description: demographics.md defaults every field to prefer not to say rather than inventing or pressing for values

checklist.name: Standing decisions recorded as comments
checklist.description: Where the user gave a rule rather than a value, it is written as a # comment above the relevant key rather than lost or buried in prose
